questions.text: Which sentence tells your own hobby?
questions.discussion: Use I like to tell an activity you enjoy.

questions.text: Rara enjoys reading storybooks. What can she say?
questions.discussion: After I like, use the activity form reading.

questions.text: Which question asks a friend about swimming?
questions.discussion: Use Do you like ...? when asking the person directly.

questions.text: Doni answers, “Yes, I do.” Which question could come before it?
questions.discussion: Yes, I do answers a Do you ...? question.

questions.text: Maya does not enjoy singing. Which answer fits “Do you like singing?”
questions.discussion: A person answering about themself uses No, I don’t.

questions.text: You ask Lila, “Do you like drawing?” She enjoys it. What should she answer?
questions.discussion: Yes, I do is the short answer to Do you ...?

questions.text: Riko says, “I like riding a bike.” Report his hobby.
questions.discussion: Use likes for one other person and keep riding.

questions.text: Complete the report: “Sinta ___ reading storybooks.”
questions.discussion: Sinta is one person, so the verb is likes.

questions.text: Two friends enjoy football. Which sentence is correct?
questions.discussion: They takes like, and the activity is playing football.

questions.text: Which question asks about one other person?
questions.discussion: Use Does + one person + like.

questions.text: Ayu’s brother enjoys swimming. How does Ayu answer “Does your brother like swimming?”
questions.discussion: He does is the short answer about Ayu’s brother.

questions.text: Beni’s sister does not enjoy dancing. Which answer fits?
questions.discussion: Use she doesn’t for one female person.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly reports a hobby?
questions.discussion: One person takes likes followed by the activity singing.

questions.text: Complete the question: “___ Made like flying a kite?”
questions.discussion: Use Does when asking about Made, one other person.

questions.text: After Does, which form is correct?
questions.discussion: Does already marks the third-person question, so the main verb stays like.

questions.text: “Does Nara like drawing?” The survey says No. Choose the report.
questions.discussion: For one other person, use doesn’t like.

questions.text: Tono likes swimming and reading. Which statement is supported?
questions.discussion: The sentence names two activities that Tono likes.

questions.text: A survey has Yes for cycling and No for dancing. Which report matches?
options: She doesn’t like cycling or dancing.
She likes cycling, but she doesn’t like dancing.
She likes dancing, but not cycling.
questions.answer: She likes cycling, but she doesn’t like dancing.
questions.discussion: Yes marks cycling as liked and No marks dancing as not liked.

questions.text: What does “hobby” mean in this unit?
options: a meal eaten in the morning
questions.discussion: Unit 4 uses hobby for an activity a person enjoys.

questions.text: Which activity needs a storybook in the unit?
questions.discussion: A storybook is used for reading.

questions.text: Which phrase names an activity with a bicycle?
questions.discussion: Riding a bike is the expression used for cycling.

questions.text: Which phrase names the team ball activity in the unit?
questions.discussion: The unit uses playing football.

questions.text: Which sentence keeps the same meaning as “Joshua enjoys swimming”?
questions.discussion: Likes swimming reports that swimming is an activity Joshua enjoys.

questions.text: You do not know whether Wati likes drawing. What should you do?
questions.discussion: A survey answer must come from Wati’s response.

questions.text: A survey cell is blank. What does the blank safely mean?
options: The answer has not been recorded.
questions.answer: The answer has not been recorded.
questions.discussion: A blank cell gives no recorded Yes or No answer.

questions.text: Rani says Yes to swimming and singing. Which report matches?
questions.discussion: Both recorded answers are Yes.

questions.text: “Do you like reading?” “No, I don’t. I like drawing.” What does the speaker like?
questions.discussion: The speaker rejects reading and then says they like drawing.

questions.text: “Does Edo like football?” “Yes, he does.” Which full sentence matches?
questions.discussion: Yes, he does confirms Edo’s football hobby.

questions.text: Nina and Sari like watching TV. Replace their names with a pronoun.
questions.discussion: They refers to Nina and Sari together.

questions.text: Which response politely gives a different hobby?
options: No, I don’t. I like reading.
questions.answer: No, I don’t. I like reading.
questions.discussion: The complete response answers No and then names the preferred hobby.

questions.text: Put the words in the correct order: like / Do / swimming / you?
questions.discussion: A yes/no question begins Do you like, then the activity.

questions.text: Correct the sentence “He like singing.”
questions.discussion: He takes likes in a statement.

questions.text: Correct the question “Does she likes dancing?”
questions.discussion: After Does, use the base form like.

questions.text: A class survey records five Yes answers for reading and two for swimming. Which hobby has more Yes answers?
questions.discussion: Five is greater than two, so reading has more Yes answers.

questions.text: A friend says, “I like swimming.” Which follow-up stays on the same topic?
options: What do you have for dinner?
Do you like swimming at the pool?
questions.answer: Do you like swimming at the pool?
questions.discussion: The follow-up still asks about the friend’s swimming hobby.
